en: The Sūtra on the Bodhisattva’s Observance of the Fast, translated by the Western Jin lay devotee Nie Daozhen.
Regarding the method for the Bodhisattva’s observance of the fast, it says: “I, [Name], take refuge in the Buddha; I take refuge in the Dharma; I take refuge in the Saṅgha.”
"O Sangha, the evil I have committed with my body, the evil I have spoken with my mouth, and the evil I have conceived in my mind have now been abandoned and discarded.

For [a certain number of] days and [a certain number of] nights, I observe the Bodhisattva fast and take refuge in the Bodhisattvas, just as the sixty thousand Bodhisattvas before me all maintained this fast."

I am a bodhisattva, like the former bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, Huṇa-kulū, Aruḍa, Dharmaka, Maitreya, A-vi-lou-shi-li, Śramaṇa-dhāru-dāna, Rā-śūraṃgama, and the bodhisattvas who possess the power of recollecting past lives, all of whom observe this fast.
I am a bodhisattva, observing the bodhisattva fast.
If I practice the giving of alms, I shall attain the dāna-pāramitā;
as I receive my prediction of enlightenment, I shall attain the vīrya-pāramitā.
By sitting in meditation with a single mind, one shall attain the dhyāna-pāramitā;

by preaching the sūtras as I have taught them, one shall attain the prajñā-pāramitā—this is called *upāya-kauśalya*. From this, one attains the *mahā-prajñā-pāramitā*, just as one contemplates those among the denizens of hell, the hungry ghosts (*preta*), and the animals, causing them to obtain liberation and be reborn as humans. From this point, by practicing the giving of alms (*dāna*), one shall reach the presence of the Buddhas Sumeru, Kruḍanda, and Amitābha, and there receive and attain the samādhis of meditation.
"This is the method for a bodhisattva to receive the fast (upavāsa).
The Buddha told Subhūti:
'A bodhisattva has ten recollections (smṛti) which they should protect.'"
What are the ten recollections?
One should recollect the Buddhas of the past; this is the Dharma of a bodhisattva.
One should recollect the Buddhas of the future; this is the Dharma of a bodhisattva.
One should mindfully recollect all Buddhas currently residing in the ten directions; this is the Dharma of a bodhisattva.
One should mindfully recollect the perfection of ethical discipline (*śīlapāramitā*) and maintain the precepts; this is the Dharma of a bodhisattva.
One should mindfully recollect the perfection of meditative concentration (*dhyānapāramitā*); this is the Dharma of a bodhisattva.
One should mindfully contemplate *upāyakauśalya* (skillful means); this is the Dharma of a bodhisattva.
One should mindfully contemplate *prajñāpāramitā* (the perfection of wisdom); this is the Dharma of a bodhisattva.
One should mindfully contemplate the sixty thousand bodhisattvas in meditative concentration (*dhyāna-samādhi*) at the abode of Amitābha Buddha; this is the Dharma of a bodhisattva.
One should mindfully recollect one’s past, future, and present preceptors and ācāryas; this is the dharma of a bodhisattva.
These constitute the ten recollections.
If there are those who resolve their minds to seek the bodhisattva path and practice meditation, they should daily contemplate these ten matters; failing to do so constitutes a defilement of conduct.
"On the days of the Bodhisattva’s fast, there are ten precepts:
First, on the days of the Bodhisattva’s fast, one must not apply cosmetics, fragrant flowers, or perfumes.
Second, on the days of the Bodhisattva’s fast, one must not engage in singing, dancing, drumming, music, or elaborate adornment."
Third, on the day of the bodhisattva’s fast, one must not lie upon a high bed.
Fourth, on the day of the bodhisattva’s fast, after midday has passed, one must not eat again.
Fifth, on the day of the Bodhisattva’s fast, one must not carry money, knives, gold, silver, or precious jewels.
Sixth, on the day of the Bodhisattva’s fast, one must not ride in a carriage or upon oxen or horses.
Seventh, on the days of the Bodhisattva fast, one must not strike one’s children, servants, or animals.

Eighth, when a Bodhisattva maintains this fast, they obtain merit through the practice of *dāna* (charitable giving). Thinking, "I am a Bodhisattva," and considering those in the realms of hell-beings, hungry ghosts, and animals, one resolves to bring them to liberation so that they may be reborn as humans. Through such acts of *dāna*, one shall reach the presence of the Buddhas Sāṃkhamati, Krakucchanda, and Amitābha, where one receives and attains the samādhis and dhyānas; this is the Bodhisattva’s method for breaking the fast.
On the day of the Bodhisattva’s fast, when it is time to retire for rest, he joins his palms before the Buddha and says:
"Today, for all those throughout the ten directions who observe the fast and precepts, may I assist them in their immeasurable peace;
today, for all those who observe the precepts, may I assist them in their immeasurable peace."
Today, for those who possess patience and who keep in mind the people of the world, I shall assist them with immeasurable peace;
today, for those who possess diligence, I shall assist them with immeasurable peace;

today, for those who possess wisdom and preach the sutras, I shall assist them with immeasurable peace. By holding this merit of sympathetic joy and exhortation, may it flow back to all humans and non-humans (*sattva*) throughout the ten directions who dwell in places of toil, suffering, and hardship, so that they may all obtain blessings, be liberated from sorrow and pain, and be reborn as humans, enjoying boundless peace, security, wealth, and happiness.
"9) On the day of the Bodhisattva’s fast, one must not witness the sweeping of the grounds.
10) On the day of the Bodhisattva’s fast, one must not consume all the food or drink from a vessel until it is empty.
11) On the day of the Bodhisattva’s fast, one must not engage in flirtatious laughter with a woman or sit on the same mat as her; the same applies to women."
"These are the ten precepts; they must not be violated, nor may one teach others to violate them, nor may one encourage others to violate them.
The Bodhisattva, explaining the method for observing the fast, said: "Namo Buddha! Namo Dharma! Namo Bhikṣusaṃgha!"
For a certain number of days and nights, one observes the Bodhisattva fast.
By practicing the giving of alms, one shall attain the dāna-pāramitā;
by observing the precepts as I do, one shall attain the śīla-pāramitā.
Just as I bring peace and security to the people of the ten directions, so shall I attain the *kṣānti-pāramitā*;
just as I receive my prediction (*vyākaraṇa*), so shall I attain the *vīrya-pāramitā*;
just as I practice dhyāna, so shall I attain the *dhyāna-pāramitā*. This is skill-in-means (*upāya-kauśalya*), such as that found in the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā*.

"Just as the Dharma-fast of the bodhisattvas consists of sixty thousand bodhisattvas spending one part of the day and night in meditation, one part reciting the scriptures, and one part lying down; this is the rule for the bodhisattva’s fast day."
One receives [the precepts] on the fourteenth day of the first month and releases them on the seventeenth;
one receives them on the eighth day of the fourth month and releases them on the fifteenth;
one receives them on the first day of the seventh month and releases them on the sixteenth.
Received on the fourteenth day of the ninth month; concluded on the sixteenth day.
The above are the days of the fast.
I take refuge in the Western Amitābha Tathāgata, the Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha, and the Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta. May the three poisons be eliminated, and may I be reborn in the Honored Land.
The land of the Pure and Honored Deity is peaceful and secure in the west;
I pray to take refuge and submit my life to serve the Unsurpassed King.
With supernatural powers and holy wisdom fully realized, he perceives and illuminates the state of my mind.
I take refuge in the Great Protectors, Unshakable for a hundred kalpas.
The Sutra on the Bodhisattva’s Observance of the Fast.
